summary: Rebecca Redwood French works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned a J.D. from the University of Washington and an LL.M. and Ph.D. from Yale, mentored by scholars including Robert A. F. Thurman. She held posts at the University of Colorado and University at Buffalo.

Reginald A. Ray is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied under teachers including Mircea Eliade and Chögyam Trungpa. Ray taught at the University of Colorado (attested 2001–2002) and served as Professor in Buddhist Studies at Naropa University (attested 2001–2006).

Reginald Horace Blyth was a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who studied at the University of London (~1921–1923). He held posts at Keijo Imperial University (~1925–1940) and Kanazawa University (~1940–1942), and taught Robert Baker Aitken.
Rei Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Waseda University from circa 1948 to 1953 and later served as a professor there from circa 1970 to 1999.
Reiho Masunaga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Kaiten Nukariya from circa 1925 to 1931 and served as a teacher at Komazawa University from circa 1930 to 1970.

Reiko Ohnuma works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Michigan (Ph.D. attested 1997) under Luis O. Gómez and Padmanabh S. Jaini. She held positions at UT Austin, the University of Alabama, and Dartmouth College.

Reimon Yuki was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo under Daijo Tokiwa (~1924–1927). He held posts at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia, Kyoto Women's University, and became professor emeritus at Tokyo and Ryukoku.

Reiner Wiehl was a philosopher who studied at the University of Nancy and Goethe University Frankfurt (Ph.D.). He served as professor of philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1969–1977) and Heidelberg University (appointed 1977), and taught John Taber.
Reinhold Grünendahl is an Indologist. He held posts at the Free University of Berlin (attested 1983) and at the Göttingen State and University Library (attested 2008).

Reinhold Klotz was a scholar of linguistics who completed his habilitation at Leipzig University (1826–1831). He served at Leipzig University as assistant professor in 1832 and as außerordentlicher Professor from 1849 to 1870, succeeding Gottfried Hermann and teaching Friedrich Max Müller.

Reinhold Niebuhr was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Elmhurst University, Eden Theological Seminary, and Yale Divinity School. He taught Masao Abe and held a post at Union Theological Seminary from circa 1928 to 1960.

Reinhold Rost was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Jena. He held posts at St Augustine's College, the Royal Asiatic Society, and served as Headlibrarian of the India Office Library (1869–1893). He also taught Caroline Rhys Davids.

Renate Syed is an Indology scholar who earned her doctorate at the University of Munich (~1974–1982). Her doctoral supervisor was Dieter Schlingloff, and she also studied under Friedrich Wilhelm and Gritli von Mitterwallner.
Renjū Akamatsu was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Chō Sanshū and held a post at Ryukoku University from circa 1899 to 1903.

René Gothóni is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki from circa 1970 to 1982, later held a post there from circa 1977 to 2014, and taught Ilkka Pyysiäinen.

René Grousset was a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian-Central Asian studies, and sinology who studied at the University of Montpellier. He taught Jeannine Auboyer and held posts at the Louvre, École du Louvre, École Libre des Sciences Politiques, Musée Guimet, and Musée Cernuschi.
René Guénon was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He completed his education at Robert-Badinter School Complex, Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour, and the University of Paris.

René de Nebesky-Wojkowitz was a Tibetology and religious studies scholar who earned his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Vienna. He also studied at SOAS, LSE, and Berlin under scholars including Giuseppe Tucci, and held a post at Weltmuseum Wien (1958).
Reting Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche and Chatral Sangye Dorje, and he taught Tenzin Gyatso.

Rewata Dhamma was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a B.A., M.A., and Ph.D. at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University between 1956 and 1967, and earned a doctorate from Banaras Hindu University (1956–1967).
